item.title: Fed's Bowman says Basel proposal still on track for end of Q1
item.description: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said in comments Wednesday that the central bank plans to publish its Basel III endgame capital proposal for public comment before the end of March.

item.title: Olympics boost spending in Italy; UK banks push Visa, Mastercard rival
item.description: The Olympics are boosting spending in Italy, large-in-part thanks to Americans. In the U.K., Barclays is reportedly leading a meeting to seek support for an existing project. The meeting comes against the backdrop of geopolitical concerns and the dominance of American-based payment firms.

item.title: Banks that won on deposit growth in 2025 got boost from M&A
item.description: Lenders with between $10 billion and $100 billion of assets grew their core deposits by more than 8% last year, or more than double the industry-wide average. Merger activity was largely responsible for the outsized growth.

item.title: Tokenized Treasuries: What happens when securities become money?
item.description: Tokenized money market funds are becoming more money-like — but, unlike the payment stablecoins that share the same backing, they are securities. Noelle Acheson looks at what this means for our understanding of money.

item.title: Warren warns Fed, Treasury against crypto bailout
item.description: Senate Banking Committee ranking member Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., warned the Treasury Department and Federal Reserve in a Wednesday letter not to bail out cryptocurrency firms in the wake of sharp declines in digital asset values over the last several months.

item.title: Global Payments' turnaround gets off on the right foot
item.description: Investors were encouraged by Global Payments' fourth-quarter earnings results – the first post WorldPay acquisition – but some analysts remained skeptical that the legacy fintech could turn its business around.

item.title: OpenClaw AI creates shadow IT risks for banks
item.description: Bank employees are likely adopting the OpenClaw AI assistant on the sly to boost productivity, but the tool's deep integration exposes networks to cyber threats.

item.title: Medallion stresses home improvement to drive 2026 growth
item.description: The New York City-based lender, whose roots lie in taxi lending, believes an expanded home-improvement loan operation will generate mid-teen loan growth this year.

item.title: Stripe-owned Bridge acquires trust charter for stablecoins
item.description: The stablecoin arm of Stripe recently announced its conditional trust charter approval from the OCC and a partnership with business payments fintech Payoneer.

item.title: M&T says Tricolor-related lawsuit could lead to losses
item.description: The Buffalo-based bank didn't specify the size of potential losses from a suit that grew out of the collapse of subprime auto lender Tricolor Holdings. M&T said its trust subsidiary will "vigorously defend itself" against claims by investors who allege that it should have protected them from alleged fraud.
